did_you_know.text: The name Massah is related to the Hebrew root meaning “to test,” while Meribah is related to the root meaning “to quarrel.” The place names therefore recall both the test and the argument.
According to Genesis, Amalek was Esau’s grandson and Eliphaz’s son. Here, Amalek first appears in the Torah as a people fighting Israel.
This is the first time Joshua is mentioned by name in the Torah. His name is connected to the Hebrew root meaning “to save” and to God’s name, expressing the idea that God saves.
The word emunah here means steadiness and persistence, not only belief. The story shows that even a strong leader needs the help of others.
The name Adonai Nissi means “The LORD is my banner.” In the ancient world, a banner served as a rallying point and encouraged soldiers.
